title: Gravitational lensing, apparent dark matter, and causal-set/causal-rewrite structural bridge register
track: Causal Step (unqualified exploratory research), separate from qualified IsoGraph and Woit/Lisi
research_origin: Joshua Oshiro identifies local gravitational lensing and its implications for dark-matter ideas as a direct comparison target for Causal Step and causal sets.
agent_contribution: AI-assisted primary-source searches, literature normalization, critical assumption audit and exact weak-field observer noninjectivity control.
scope: Lensing observations and source-independent structural comparison, not proposal that dark matter does not exist or a derivation of spacetime from source hypergraphs.

entries.name: One gravitational potential or two? Forecasts and tests
entries.evidence: Relativistic massless probes respond to time and spatial potentials; massive dynamics tests time potential; joint test gravitational slip.
entries.assumption: Perturbed relativistic metric, galaxy physics and measured distance/redshift/source effects; no pregeometry.

entries.name: Modified Einstein versus modified Euler for dark matter
entries.evidence: An effective measured gravitational slip can mimic modified gravity even if a fifth force affects dark matter dynamics; lensing-vs-dynamics alone not uniquely diagnostic.
entries.assumption: Cosmological linear perturbation and tracer response models; need independent potential/geodesic-redshift constraints.

entries.name: A direct empirical proof of the existence of dark matter
entries.evidence: Bullet Cluster merger X-ray gas vs lensing gravitational mass/growth peaks spatially offset; strong cluster-morphology falsifier.
entries.assumption: Weak-lensing inversion, baryonic X-ray mapping, projection/distance; dark matter particle ontology inference is not uniquely built into the photons.

entries.name: Radial acceleration relation of galaxies with joint kinematic and weak-lensing data
entries.authors: T. Mistele, S. McGaugh, F. Lelli, J. Schombert and P. Li
entries.evidence: Weak-lensing inferred radial acceleration continues the galaxy kinematic RAR over ~2.5 dex lower g; joint baryon-dynamics-lensing comparison.
entries.assumption: Mass-to-light ratio, isolation, source redshift, profile deprojection and metric-lensing-to-acceleration conversion.

entries.name: The weak lensing radial acceleration relation: constraining modified gravity and cold dark matter theories with KiDS-1000
entries.evidence: Agreement with some MOND/EG-inspired mean trends and substantial galaxy-type differences; data/systematics and hidden circumgalactic gas matter.
entries.assumption: Galaxy sample cuts, source-mass modeling, morphological gas environment; contrast with 2024 Mistele strict-isolation result, do not simply choose whichever confirms a hypothesis.

entries.name: The Bullet Cluster evidence shows modified gravity in the absence of dark matter
entries.authors: J. R. Brownstein and J. W. Moffat
entries.evidence: Published modified-gravity competing fit to Bullet Cluster lensing/gas arrangement, not an established unique solution.
entries.assumption: Specific additional modified-gravity dynamics, baryonic component distribution and model fitting; cannot transfer to Causal Step without reconstruction.

entries.name: On the proof of dark matter, the law of gravity and the mass of neutrinos
entries.authors: G. W. Angus, H. Shan, H. Zhao, B. Famaey
entries.evidence: Under another MOND-like lensing treatment, colliding clusters still require collisionless matter; directly disputes blanket claims baryonic modified gravity suffices.
entries.assumption: Specific modified gravity interpolation and lens reconstruction; historical neutrino model options not current empirical proof.

entries.name: An ultra-high-resolution map of (dark) matter
entries.evidence: JWST COSMOS-Web weak-lensing map with ~1 arcminute resolution, 129 lensed galaxies per arcmin2; filaments/cluster structure, toward redshift 2.
entries.assumption: Source shape measurements, shear calibration and reconstruction using cosmological distance models; map is effective lensing mass reconstruction, not a particle photograph.

entries.name: Measurement of the Minimum Cold Dark Matter Halo Mass with Strong Gravitational Lensing
entries.evidence: 28 strong lenses constrain the lower halo-mass-function cutoff in a specified CDM model to less than 10^8.2-8.3 solar masses at 10:1 odds, with simulation priors.
entries.assumption: Lensing mass profiles, subhalo mass function and concentration/stripping assumptions; not a particle mass measurement.

entries.name: First measurement of narrow-line flux ratios for a lensed quasar with JWST/NIRSpec integral field spectroscopy
entries.evidence: September 2026 accepted study measures ~5% quasar narrow-line flux-ratio errors and a cusp anomaly relative to smooth lens model; baryon-free gravitational substructure probe.
entries.assumption: Macro lens model, source emission sizes and offsets, stellar microlensing suppression, line-of-sight structures; no unique dark-subhalo inference from one anomaly.

entries.name: The BUFFALO Survey: The Subhalo Mass Function for Abell 2744 with Strong+Weak Gravitational Lensing
entries.evidence: October 6 2026 preprint combines HST/JWST strong+weak lensing and finds substructure excess against BAHAMAS in a highly disturbed merging cluster.
entries.assumption: Authors favor unrelaxed merger environment rather than simple tension with CDM/SIDM; sample-size/dynamical-state caveats load bearing.

entries.name: Essentials of Strong Gravitational Lensing
entries.authors: Prasenjit Saha, Dominique Sluse, Jenny Wagner and Liliya L. R. Williams
entries.evidence: Inverse lensing reconstruction generally nonunique; mass-sheet and local-observable degeneracies must be treated as first-class observational equivalence problems.
entries.assumption: Different source positions, mass profiles, distances and external shear can give same images; additional kinematics/time-delay data can help.

entries.name: The causal set approach to quantum gravity
entries.evidence: Causal sets are locally finite posets; under manifoldlike continuum approximation, causal order constrains conformal geometry while element count supplies volume.
entries.assumption: No arbitrary higher-order native hypergraph rewrite history is automatically a causal set or a faithful manifoldlike sprinkling.

entries.name: Null geodesics in conformal gravity
entries.authors: G. E. Turner and K. Horne
entries.evidence: Null geodesic unparameterized curves and causal cone structure preserved under smooth positive conformal metric rescaling.
entries.assumption: Requires a Lorentzian metric and photon-geometric-optics limit; time delays, focusing scalar quantities and massive trajectories need separate treatment.

entries.name: Local d'Alembertian for causal sets
entries.evidence: Constructs local discrete wave operator converging for arbitrary fields in Minkowski causets, addressing some nonlocal operator issues.
entries.assumption: Faithful causal-set realization and Minkowski continuum are assumed for convergence; does NOT derive galactic/cluster lensing, curvature or higher-order rewrite equivalence.

entries.name: Discreteness and the transmission of light from distant sources
entries.authors: F. Dowker, J. Henson, R. D. Sorkin
entries.evidence: Causal-set sourced/detected massless scalar transmission on preexisting causal set backgrounds can approximate continuum propagation.
entries.assumption: Not an electromagnetic lensing prediction through a dynamically emerged curved spacetime.

entries.name: A test of general relativity using radio links with the Cassini spacecraft
entries.authors: B. Bertotti, L. Iess, P. Tortora
entries.evidence: Solar-system Shapiro delay near the Sun constrains PPN gamma-1=(2.1±2.3)×10^-5, providing a high-acceleration local control.
entries.assumption: Effective PPN metric regime; constrains theories predicting wrong local light response without preventing environment-dependent effects outside Solar System.

entries.name: Strong Gravitational Lensing as a Probe of Dark Matter
entries.authors: S. Vegetti, S. Birrer, G. Despali, C. D. Fassnacht, D. Gilman, Y. Hezaveh, L. Perreault Levasseur, J. P. McKean, D. M. Powell, C. M. O'Riordan and G. Vernardos
entries.evidence: Review of small-scale strong lensing dark-substructure inference and macro-model degeneracies.
entries.assumption: Flux-anomaly subhalo inference depends on mass models, magnification, source structure and baryonic systematics.

entries.name: The mass-sheet degeneracy and time-delay cosmography
entries.evidence: κ_lambda=λκ+(1−λ) produces indistinguishable image positions after rescaling source position; lens mass inverse is not generically injective.
entries.assumption: Thin lens equation and free source scale, independent time-delays/dynamics/line-of-sight calibration can break or change degeneracy.

entries.name: Causal sets and an emerging continuum
entries.evidence: Many nonmanifoldlike causal sets are suppressed under selected gravitational path-integral weights, but manifoldlike continuum emergence is not completed.
entries.assumption: Adopted gravitational path integral / causal-set action; not a result for arbitrary growing rank-k hypergraphs.

entries.name: Energy-momentum diffusion from spacetime discreteness
entries.authors: L. Philpott, F. Dowker and R. D. Sorkin
entries.evidence: Phenomenological Lorentz-invariant drift/diffusion bounds for massive and massless particle motion on specific causal-set backgrounds.
entries.assumption: Assumes background approximates Minkowski and particle dynamics with introduced parameters; not a derived curved lensing model.

priority_order: 1. Null-geodesic/conformal geometry and causal-order information sufficiency
2. Two-potential lensing-versus-dynamical test with local PPN and galaxy RAR joint data
3. Lensing inverse noninjectivity/mass-sheet ambiguity against causal model coarse observers
4. Cluster gas/galaxy/lensing offsets and merger-time conditional event histories
5. Fine subhalo-scale anomalies, cosmic shear and CMB lensing if lower tiers become predictive
negative_constraints: Mass maps are reconstructions of lensing observables under effective geometry/cosmological assumptions, not direct evidence specifying particle identity.
Do not assume a force law, background dimensional space, Einstein metric, speed of light or dark-matter field as fundamental causal rewrite primitives.
Do not force every competing modified-gravity fit to fail by definition; test joint multi-probe evidence, including cases where extra collisionless matter still seems required.
Do not equate a causal set partially ordered manifold approximation with the native unordered genuine k-way event rewrite generator.
Do not interpret observed strong-lens anomalous fluxes as unique detection of a subhalo without macro lens/stellar microlensing/source-size uncertainty.
Neither local bending agreement nor a single galactic RAR fit proves the physical origin of the gravitational response.
